original_question: Do any genes associated with Cystinuria syndrome encode proteins that belong to a family of light subunit amino acid transporters?

final_qi.question: Do any genes associated with Cystinuria syndrome encode proteins that belong to a family of light subunit amino acid transporters?
final_qi.long_answer: Cystinuria is most commonly caused by pathogenic variants in two genes: SLC3A1 and SLC7A9. SLC3A1 encodes rBAT, the heavy subunit of the renal cystine–dibasic amino-acid transporter. SLC7A9 encodes b0,+AT, which is the light subunit of the same heteromeric transporter complex and is a member of the SLC7 family of light subunit amino-acid transporters (heteromeric amino-acid transporter family, HAT). Thus, at least one cystinuria-associated gene (SLC7A9) clearly encodes a protein that belongs to the family of light subunit amino-acid transporters. Therefore, the statement is supported by established biomedical consensus.
